transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. My mind keeps drifting off in meetings and calls, and I get distracted so easily that it’s starting to hurt my performance as a supervisor. I'm really struggling to stay mentally present when it matters most, and I need to figure out what's going on.
Did you experience these difficulties with focus and concentration during your childhood, or is this a relatively new problem for you?

No, this definitely isn't new; I've actually struggled with this since I was a kid. Even back in elementary school, my teachers always wrote on my report cards that I daydreamed in class, forgot to turn in homework I'd finished, and couldn't stay in my seat without talking or fidgeting. It's really been a lifelong pattern for me.
Beyond the difficulty with focus, do you frequently feel an internal sense of restlessness, or do you often find yourself interrupting others or acting before thinking?

Yes, I definitely do. In long meetings, I get this internal buzzing feeling like I'm crawling out of my skin, so I'm constantly shifting around and bouncing my leg just to cope. I also have a bad habit of interrupting people, cutting them off to finish their sentences or blurting out answers before they've even finished the question.
Do you find that these difficulties with staying focused and the restlessness affect you consistently in both your work environment and your home life or personal relationships?

Yes, it definitely impacts both areas of my life. At work, I've been written up for missing details and my boss is questioning my readiness for promotion, which means I'm constantly staying late to fix mistakes. That leaves me with much less time to spend with my son, and I'm falling behind on everyday things like paying bills and handling my divorce paperwork.
